annotations.title: Missing right mudra
annotations.lead: Like most other free standing sculptures of Vairochana, the right hand has broken off. We can use other references from the time period to try and learn how the hand might have been posed.

annotations.title: Fossil fragments
annotations.lead: Some fossil fragments are evident in the weathered surface of the Buddha.

annotations.title: Base of the Cosmic Buddha
annotations.lead: The Cosmic Buddha was set into a concrete base in 1971 to secure the heavy sculpture (over 800 pounds) for exhibition.

annotations.title: Lion Spirit King
annotations.lead: Lion Spirit King (shizi shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Dragon Spirit King
annotations.lead: Dragon Spirit King (long shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Pearl Spirit King
annotations.lead: Pearl Spirit King (zhu shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Fire Spirit King
annotations.lead: Fire Spirit King (huo shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Wind Spirit King
annotations.lead: Wind Spirit King (feng shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Fish Spirit King
annotations.lead: Fish Spirit King (yu shenwang), one of the ten Spirit Kings

annotations.title: Evidence of recarving
annotations.lead: This area exemplifies a recarved surface of the Cosmic Buddha. On the opposite side of the figure the hotspot "Weathering of the carved surface" provides a clear comparison between the original and recarved stone.

annotations.title: Low relief carving
annotations.lead: Scene on front waist where edges of the low relief carving are less sharp and more polished due to damage caused largely by the rubbing process previously used to document the Cosmic Buddha over its many years.

annotations.title: Weathering of the carved surface
annotations.lead: Natural weathering, which occurred after the sculpture was carved, has softened the details of the carving.

annotations.title: Missing left mudra
annotations.lead: Though the original pendant hand of this sculpture is missing, we can use clues from similar sculptures of the time to guess how it might have have looked.

annotations.title: Petrographic analysis
annotations.lead: Samples were taken from the Cosmic Buddha to study using thin section petrography.

annotations.title: Paint remains
annotations.lead: Beige clay-based paint over a ground layer on the back of the Cosmic Buddha

annotations.title: Weathering of the stone surface
annotations.lead: The Buddha’s surface is substantially weathered, which would be expected for a sculpture exposed to the natural elements or buried in soil for centuries.

annotations.title: Summit of Sumeru
annotations.lead: Sumeru, “wonderful [mount] Meru”

annotations.title: Devas of Trayashrimsha
annotations.lead: The 8 figures to the left and right of the Historical Buddha Shakyamuni are Devas of Trayashrimsha

annotations.title: Historical Buddha Shakyamuni
annotations.lead: The Historical Buddha Shakyamunihe is depicted seated on a lotus, his right hand is raised in a gesture of teaching (vitarka mudra) while his left hand rests in his lap with the palm upwards.

annotations.title: Apsaras
annotations.lead: The four figures surrounding the scene on the summit of Sumeru are Apsaras.

annotations.title: The Six Realms of Existence in Buddhist cosmology
annotations.lead: The scenes on the front of the sculpture depict units of the Realm of Desire (Kamadhatu), one of three Buddhist worlds. The Realm of Desire ranges from the underworld to heaven.

tours.title: Buddhas on the Buddha
tours.lead: Among the hundreds of figures carved on the Cosmic Buddha are depictions of Dipankara (Buddha of the Distant Past), Shakyamuni (the Historical Buddha), and the bodhisattva Maitreya, the Buddha of the Future. They are often called “Buddhas of the Three Eras” in Chinese Buddhism.

titles.EN: Chinese Buddhist Sculpture in the Opening Installation at the Freer Gallery of Art in May 1923
Metal Rod Added at the Neck

tours.lead: This tour shares archival photographs taken in 1923 to discuss the purchase of the sculpture in Beijing, the condition of its surface when it arrived in Washington, and its place in the Freer Gallery’s collection.

titles.EN: Shakyamuni, the Historical Buddha, and His Visit to Vaishali to See Vimalakirti

tours.title: Vimalakirti Nirdesha
tours.lead: One of the most complex narrative scenes on the surface of the Cosmic Buddha illustrates the popular Vimalakirti Nirdesha sutra which recounts a meeting between Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom, and the Buddhist layman Vimalakirti.

tours.title: Missing features and absent mudras
tours.lead: This sculpture was damaged sometime in the past 1500 years resulting in the loss of its original head and hands. Now, it is only possible to suggest its original symbolic hand gestures (known as mudras in Sanskrit) through comparisons with other sculptures.
